notes: Five prompts, one per category, chosen to differentiate model strengths without taking long to run.
No system prompt is sent. Results reflect each model's default behaviour, not a harness-imposed persona.
All prompts are text-only. A multimodal model is measured on its text path here; its vision path is not benchmarked.
max_tokens is a ceiling, not a target. Reasoning models spend a large share of their budget before the answer starts.

prompts.prompt: A shop sells notebooks in packs of 4 and pens in packs of 6. A customer buys the same number of packs of each and ends up with 12 more pens than notebooks. How many packs of each did they buy, and how many pens is that in total? Show your reasoning, then state the final answer on its own line.

Summarise the following passage in exactly three bullet points.

A journaling filesystem records its intended changes in a dedicated log before applying them to the main structures on disk. If power is lost partway through a write, the system consults that log at mount time and either replays the entries that were fully recorded or discards the ones that were not. This turns a potentially arbitrary amount of post-crash repair work into a bounded operation, because the log has a fixed size and the recovery pass only has to read it once. The tradeoff is write amplification: metadata is written twice, once to the journal and once to its final location. Some filesystems narrow this cost by journaling only metadata and not file contents, which keeps the structures consistent while accepting that the tail of a file being written during a crash may be lost.
